rationale: Tests understanding of the distinction between somatic death and cellular death — the foundational FM2.3 competency on defining death
Tests understanding of the three modes of death — FM2.7 covers asphyxia, syncope, and coma as modes
Tests understanding of the medicolegal classification of death by manner — distinguishing natural from unnatural, which drives reporting obligations
Tests knowledge of legal obligations when an unnatural death is encountered — FM2.6 covers reporting requirements
Tests knowledge of rigor mortis timings — FM2.9 requires knowing PM change timelines, and the temperature caveat is a key factual requirement
Tests application of PM change interpretation — FM2.10 requires integrating multiple PM findings for PMI estimation
Tests application of MCCD Part I causal chain logic — FM2.1 requires completing the MCCD correctly using the WHO causal sequence
Tests understanding of when an MCCD cannot be issued and a coroner/police referral is required — FM2.2 competency on death certification limits
Tests recall of key THOTA 1994 provisions — FM2.4 requires knowing the legal framework for organ transplantation in India
Tests understanding of India's opt-in consent model under THOTA — a key ethical and legal feature of the Act
